::: {.ter-project-brief}
## Design brief

Identify a small genuine need that additive manufacturing can address appropriately. Design a functional part such as a bracket, adapter, spacer, knob, cable guide, tool holder, enclosure feature, assembly connector, or low-risk repair component. Print a focused prototype, test it, and revise the model.
:::

## Required evidence

- situation, user, need, requirements, and restrictions;
- measurements and the source of critical dimensions;
- alternatives and justification for using 3D printing;
- editable CAD model and exported manufacturing file;
- orientation and slicer decisions with a toolpath preview;
- a fit or feature test where uncertainty is high;
- observations from realistic use;
- at least one model revision tied to evidence.

## Appropriate scope

Avoid parts whose failure could cause injury, electrical hazard, vehicle failure, uncontrolled motion, or significant property damage unless a qualified local process explicitly supports the application. A classroom prototype is evidence for learning, not an automatic certification for service.

## Evaluate process as well as part

Consider material used, support waste, print time, failed attempts, repairability, and whether another process or an off-the-shelf component would better meet the need.

::: {.ter-curriculum-relevance}
**Ontario curriculum relevance:** Adaptable to **TIJ1O**, **TDJ2O**, **TMJ2O**, **TEJ2O**, and senior technology courses where CAD, additive manufacturing, technical problem solving, prototyping, and evaluation authentically fit the project.
:::
